heading: Questions? We can read your mind

items.q: What is BBA in Business Analytics?
a: The BBA / BBA (Hons.) in Business Analytics at ATLAS ISME is designed for aspiring data strategists who can transform complex information into actionable business intelligence. The program builds a strong foundation in data analytics, visualisation and business decision sciences, delivered through real-world datasets, live projects, AI-driven case studies and industry masterclasses.

items.q: What is the highest package in BBA Business Analytics?
a: The website does not specify package figures. However, graduates are placed across high-growth roles in data analytics, consulting, fintech and marketing analytics, sectors known for strong starting salaries in India's corporate landscape, especially from a campus located in Mumbai's BKC.

items.q: What are BBA Business Analytics subjects?
a: Key subjects include Statistics for Business, Data Visualisation & Reporting with Power BI, Analytics Using Jamovi & R Programming, Financial Analytics with Excel & R, Marketing & Retail Analytics, Social Media & Web Analytics, HR Analytics & Workforce Insights, Advanced Predictive Analytics & Business Modelling, Customer & Market Intelligence and an Industry Analytics Lab.

items.q: Is a BBA in Business Analytics good?
a: Yes. It's one of the most future-relevant business degrees available today. At ATLAS ISME, the program combines business fundamentals with data tools and AI-driven applications, preparing students for roles that are in high demand across virtually every industry.

items.q: Does BBA Business Analytics have maths?
a: Yes, but it's applied rather than purely theoretical. The curriculum includes Statistics for Business, Quantitative Methods, Financial Analytics and Predictive Modelling. The focus is on using data to solve real business problems, not advanced pure mathematics. The eligibility requires only 50% in Class XII in any stream. Maths is not mandatory for admission.

items.q: What are the top 3 skills for a business analyst?
a: Based on the ATLAS ISME curriculum and program focus, the top three skills are: data analysis and statistical thinking, data visualisation and reporting (translating insights into decisions) and strategic business modelling (connecting data to business outcomes). The program specifically trains students in all three through live projects and tool-based learning.

items.q: What jobs can I get after a BBA in Business Analytics?
a: Graduates can pursue roles such as Business / Data Analyst, Product / Data Insights Analyst, Marketing / CRM Analyst, Financial / Revenue Analyst, Supply Chain / Demand Analyst, People / HR Analyst and Analytics Consultant, across corporates, consulting firms, startups and their own ventures.

items.q: Do I need to know coding for BBA Business Analytics?
a: No prior coding knowledge is required for admission. The curriculum introduces coding through practical subjects like R Programming for Business and Python / R Programming as electives, taught from scratch with a business application focus. The emphasis is always on using code as a tool, not becoming a developer.

items.q: What tools do BBA Business Analytics students learn?
a: Students learn Power BI, Tableau, R Programming, Jamovi, Excel (advanced and financial), Python / R (as electives), SPSS and AI-enabled MarTech & AdTech tools. These are all industry-standard platforms actively used by analysts across sectors.

items.q: Can Commerce students apply for BBA Business Analytics?
a: Yes. The eligibility for the BBA in Business Analytics at ATLAS ISME requires a minimum 50% in Class XII in any stream, Commerce, Science or Arts are all accepted. No specific subject background is required to apply.

items.q: Does ATLAS ISME allow student-led startups to officially register as MSMEs?
a: Yes, ATLAS SkillTech University allows student-led startups to officially register as MSMEs. The university treats innovation as a core part of learning, encouraging students to become entrepreneurs and create real-world impact during their academic journey.

Many student-led startups at ATLAS are registered with the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India. These ventures span areas like technology, design, sustainability, education, food innovation and social entrepreneurship.

The university supports students through mentorship, industry partnerships, seed funding and incubation. Its learning model promotes risk-taking, experimentation and continuous learning, helping students turn ideas into sustainable businesses.
These startups not only contribute to the economy but also solve real-world problems, reflecting the university's focus on building future entrepreneurs and innovators.

items.q: Is there any entrepreneurship program at ATLAS ISME?
a: Yes, ATLAS ISME offers entrepreneurship programs for both undergraduate and postgraduate students. The institute focuses on developing future entrepreneurs by providing the resources, knowledge and skills needed to succeed in today's competitive business world. Through initiatives like the Entrepreneurship Lab, Startup Incubation Program and global exposure opportunities, students can build, test and refine their business ideas.

As an innovation- and entrepreneurship-driven business school, ATLAS ISME equips students with the right skills, mentorship and ecosystem to launch real-world startups even during their undergraduate journey.

From day one, students are part of an entrepreneurial environment that includes hands-on learning in marketing, design, branding, finance and e-commerce, along with exposure to real investors, industry mentors and successful founders. They also get opportunities to present their startup ideas to industry leaders in India's corporate hub.

items.q: Can I launch a startup while studying at ATLAS ISME?
a: Yes, ATLAS ISME focuses on building strong entrepreneurial skills. The curriculum prepares students for real VC pitches and helps them explore startup ideas, supported by incubation and mentorship.

Many students have already launched real startups during their time at ATLAS. Through industry-focused and hands-on learning, along with platforms like Startup Street, MVP Showcases, D2C Challenges and VC demo days, students can ideate, build and sell products while studying.
Faculty provide end-to-end support, guiding students from idea development to launching and pitching to investors.

items.q: What is the D2C challenge at ATLAS ISME?
a: The D2C Challenge at ATLAS ISME is a unique program where students build and scale their own brands, mentored by Arjun Vaidya, co-founder of V3 Ventures and a leading D2C entrepreneur in India.

It goes beyond a competition and offers a complete, hands-on startup journey. Students attend expert sessions on branding, e-commerce and strategy, gain access to Arjun's D2C playbook and receive real-time mentorship. They also work in teams to build products and get opportunities to pitch to investors and take their ideas to market.
It is one of many initiatives at ATLAS ISME that help students launch real businesses.

items.q: What is the MVP showcase at ATLAS ISME?
a: The MVP Showcase at ATLAS ISME highlights the minimum viable products (MVPs) created by students.

As an innovation-driven business school, ATLAS ISME provides the skills, mentorship and ecosystem needed to launch real-world startups during the undergraduate journey. This is reflected in the MVP Showcase, where students present practical, real-world solutions built from their ideas.

Students get the opportunity to present their startup ideas to venture capitalists, startup founders and CEOs, demonstrating their entrepreneurial mindset and business skills. From identifying real-world problems to building MVPs, students create solutions across sectors like fashion, food, SaaS and social impact.

items.q: Can non-business students, i.e. B.Sc. Finance students, also participate in entrepreneurship activities?
a: Yes, absolutely. ATLAS ISME promotes entrepreneurship across all disciplines.

Whether a student is from a B.Sc. Finance or any other background, like design or technology, at ATLAS SkillTech University, they can participate in entrepreneurship activities. Students get access to the D2C Challenge, Startup Street, mentorship programs and innovation labs, all designed to help them turn their ideas into real ventures.
